iam.diagram:
flowchart TD r[API request]:::user --> a@svc(iam, "IAM evaluates
all policies") a --> q1{"Explicit Deny
anywhere?"}:::note q1 -->|yes| deny[DENY]:::sec q1 -->|no| q2{"SCP and RCP
allow?"}:::note q2 -->|no| deny q2 -->|yes| q3{"Permissions boundary /
session policy allow?"}:::note q3 -->|no| deny q3 -->|yes| q4{"Identity or resource
policy allows?"}:::note q4 -->|no| deny q4 -->|yes| allow[ALLOW]:::storage
iam.diagramCaption: Default is implicit deny: an explicit Deny anywhere wins, and an Allow only counts if SCPs/RCPs, boundaries and session policies all permit it too.

iam-identity-center.diagram:
flowchart TD u[Workforce users]:::user --> idp[Entra ID / Okta]:::ext idp -->|SAML + SCIM| ic@svc(iam-identity-center) ic --> ps[Permission sets]:::note subgraph org[AWS Organization] a1[Prod account
role]:::sec a2[Dev account
role]:::sec end ps -->|provisions roles| a1 ps -->|provisions roles| a2 ic -->|SSO| app[SaaS apps]:::ext
iam-identity-center.diagramCaption: One workforce login federated from your IdP; permission sets become IAM roles in every account, so there are no IAM users to manage.

organizations.diagram:
flowchart TD root@svc(organizations, "Root + mgmt") root --> sec[Security OU
SCP]:::sec root --> wl[Workloads OU
SCP]:::sec root --> more[More OUs ...]:::note sec --> la[Log archive,
Audit]:::user wl --> prod[Prod OU]:::note prod --> p1[App account]:::user
organizations.diagramCaption: SCPs attach to OUs and are inherited downward; they cap permissions for everyone in member accounts (even root) but never grant any.

control-tower.diagram:
flowchart TD ct@svc(control-tower) --> org@svc(organizations, "Landing zone OUs") ct --> af[Account Factory]:::note ct --> ctl[Controls:
preventive / detective / proactive]:::sec ct --> ic@svc(iam-identity-center, "SSO") af --> na[New account]:::user subgraph secou[Security OU] log@svc(cloudtrail, "Log archive
org trail") aud@svc(config, "Audit
Config") end na -->|logs| log na -->|config| aud ctl -.->|SCPs, Config rules, Hooks| na
control-tower.diagramCaption: Control Tower assembles Organizations, Identity Center, CloudTrail and Config into a governed landing zone and vends new accounts with guardrails already on.

kms.diagram:
flowchart TD app@svc(lambda, "App") app -->|GenerateDataKey| kms@svc(kms, "KMS key") kms --> dk[Plaintext +
wrapped data key]:::note dk -->|encrypt locally| enc[Encrypted data]:::storage enc --> s3@svc(s3) dk -.->|store wrapped key| s3 s3 -.->|read: Decrypt key| kms
kms.diagramCaption: Envelope encryption: KMS only encrypts small data keys; your data is encrypted locally and the wrapped key is stored next to it.

secrets-manager.diagram:
flowchart TD app@svc(lambda, "App") app -->|GetSecretValue
cached| sm@svc(secrets-manager) sm -->|decrypt| kms@svc(kms) sm -->|every 30 days| rot@svc(lambda, "Rotation
function") rot -->|set new password| db@svc(rds) rot -->|store new version| sm app -->|connect| db
secrets-manager.diagramCaption: Apps fetch credentials at runtime; Secrets Manager rotates them on a schedule with a rotation function, so nothing is hard-coded.

cognito.diagram:
flowchart TD u[Mobile / web user]:::user -->|sign in| up@svc(cognito, "User pool") up -.->|federate| soc[Google / Apple / SAML]:::ext up -->|JWT tokens| u u -->|Bearer JWT| apigw@svc(api-gateway) apigw -->|authorizer validates| up apigw --> fn@svc(lambda) u -->|exchange JWT| ip@svc(cognito, "Identity pool") ip -->|temp AWS creds| s3@svc(s3, "Direct S3
upload")
cognito.diagramCaption: User pools authenticate customers and issue JWTs; identity pools exchange those tokens for temporary IAM credentials to call AWS directly.

waf.diagram:
flowchart TD u[Clients and bots]:::user --> cf@svc(cloudfront) cf --> waf@svc(waf, "Web ACL") waf --> rules[Rules: managed SQLi/XSS,
rate-based, Bot Control]:::sec rules -->|allowed| alb@svc(elb, "ALB") rules -.->|blocked 403| x[Blocked]:::note alb --> app@svc(ecs)
waf.diagramCaption: WAF inspects layer-7 requests at CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway or AppSync and blocks exploits, floods and bots before they reach your app.

shield.diagram:
flowchart TD atk[DDoS traffic]:::ext --> r53@svc(route53) atk --> cf@svc(cloudfront) subgraph edge[AWS edge] std[Shield Standard
L3/L4, free, automatic]:::sec adv@svc(shield, "Shield Advanced") end cf --- std cf --- adv adv --> srt[Shield Response Team
+ cost protection]:::note adv --> waf@svc(waf, "Auto L7
mitigation") cf --> alb@svc(elb, "Origin ALB")
shield.diagramCaption: Everyone gets Shield Standard at the edge; Advanced adds L7 auto-mitigation via WAF, 24/7 SRT access and DDoS cost protection.

guardduty.diagram:
flowchart TD ct@svc(cloudtrail, "CloudTrail events") --> gd@svc(guardduty) fl@svc(vpc, "VPC Flow Logs") --> gd more[DNS, EKS, S3,
RDS, runtime ...]:::note --> gd gd -->|findings| sh@svc(security-hub) gd -->|findings| eb@svc(eventbridge) eb --> fn@svc(lambda, "Auto-remediate
isolate instance") eb --> sns@svc(sns, "Notify SecOps")
guardduty.diagramCaption: GuardDuty reads logs you already have, with no agents or appliances, and emits threat findings you route through EventBridge for automated response.

security-hub.diagram:
flowchart TD gd@svc(guardduty) --> sh@svc(security-hub, "Security Hub
delegated admin") in@svc(inspector) --> sh more[Macie, Config CSPM,
partners ...]:::note --> sh sh --> risk[Correlated risks
and exposures]:::note risk --> eb@svc(eventbridge) eb --> tk[Ticketing / SOAR]:::ext
security-hub.diagramCaption: Security Hub is the single pane: it aggregates and correlates findings from every account and service, then prioritizes exposures for response.

inspector.diagram:
flowchart TD ins@svc(inspector) ins -->|agent or agentless| ec2@svc(ec2) ins -->|on push + continuous| ecr@svc(ecr) ins -->|packages + code| fn@svc(lambda) ec2 --> cve[CVE and network
reachability findings]:::note ecr --> cve fn --> cve cve --> sh@svc(security-hub) cve --> ssm@svc(systems-manager, "Patch Manager")
inspector.diagramCaption: Inspector continuously scans EC2, container images and Lambda for known vulnerabilities; feed findings to Security Hub and patch with Systems Manager.

macie.diagram:
flowchart TD s3a@svc(s3, "Data lake bucket") --> mc@svc(macie) s3b@svc(s3, "Uploads bucket") --> mc mc --> id[Managed + custom
data identifiers]:::note mc -->|PII found| f[Sensitive data
findings]:::sec mc -->|bucket posture| p[Public / unencrypted
buckets]:::sec f --> sh@svc(security-hub) f --> eb@svc(eventbridge)
macie.diagramCaption: Macie samples and classifies S3 objects to find PII and flags risky bucket settings, so you know where sensitive data lives.

cloudtrail.diagram:
flowchart TD subgraph org[Member accounts] a1[Account A API calls]:::user a2[Account B API calls]:::user end a1 --> ct@svc(cloudtrail, "Organization trail") a2 --> ct ct --> s3@svc(s3, "Log archive bucket
Object Lock") ct --> cw@svc(cloudwatch, "CloudWatch Logs") ct --> eb@svc(eventbridge, "Real-time rules") s3 --> ath@svc(athena, "Investigate")
cloudtrail.diagramCaption: One organization trail writes every account's API calls to an immutable log-archive bucket; management events are free, data events cost extra.

config.diagram:
flowchart TD res[EC2, S3, SG, IAM...
resource changes]:::user --> cfg@svc(config, "Config recorder") cfg --> hist[Configuration history
and timeline]:::note cfg --> rule{"Rule: EBS
encrypted?"}:::note rule -->|compliant| ok[Compliant]:::storage rule -->|noncompliant| rem@svc(systems-manager, "SSM Automation
remediation") rule --> agg[Aggregator
all accounts]:::mgmt
config.diagramCaption: Config records what every resource looked like over time and evaluates rules against it; pair noncompliant results with SSM auto-remediation.

acm.diagram:
flowchart TD acm@svc(acm) -->|DNS validation| r53@svc(route53) acm -->|auto-renew| cert[Public TLS cert
free]:::sec cert --> cf@svc(cloudfront, "CloudFront
cert in us-east-1") cert --> alb@svc(elb, "ALB HTTPS listener") cert --> apigw@svc(api-gateway) pca[Private CA]:::sec -.->|internal certs| acm
acm.diagramCaption: ACM issues and auto-renews public certificates for integrated services at no cost; CloudFront certificates must live in us-east-1.

detective.diagram:
flowchart TD gd@svc(guardduty, "Finding: unusual
API calls") --> dt@svc(detective) ct@svc(cloudtrail) --> dt more[Flow Logs,
EKS audit logs ...]:::note --> dt dt --> g[Behavior graph
role, IPs, resources]:::note g --> an[Analyst: scope and
root cause]:::user
detective.diagramCaption: Detective turns logs into a behavior graph so you can investigate a GuardDuty finding: who did what, from where, and what else they touched.

security-lake.diagram:
flowchart TD ct@svc(cloudtrail) --> sl@svc(security-lake) fl@svc(vpc, "Flow Logs") --> sl more[Resolver logs, Security Hub,
third-party ...]:::note --> sl sl -->|OCSF Parquet| s3@svc(s3, "Your S3 data lake") s3 --> ath@svc(athena, "Query") s3 --> siem[SIEM subscribers]:::ext
security-lake.diagramCaption: Security Lake normalizes security logs from all accounts into OCSF in your own S3, so any analytics tool or SIEM can subscribe.

verified-access.diagram:
flowchart TD u[Remote employee
no VPN]:::user -->|HTTPS| va@svc(verified-access) va -->|who?| ic@svc(iam-identity-center, "Identity provider") va -->|device healthy?| dev[Device posture
CrowdStrike / Jamf]:::ext va --> pol{"Cedar policy
allows?"}:::note subgraph vpc[VPC private subnet] app@svc(elb, "Internal app ALB") end pol -->|yes| app
verified-access.diagramCaption: Verified Access applies zero trust: every request is checked against identity and device posture policies before reaching a private app, with no VPN.

bedrock.diagram:
flowchart TD u[User question]:::user --> app@svc(lambda, "App") app --> g1@svc(bedrock, "Guardrails
input check") g1 --> kb@svc(bedrock, "Knowledge Base
retrieve") kb --> vs@svc(opensearch, "Vector store") docs@svc(s3, "Docs in S3") -->|ingest + embed| kb kb -->|context chunks| fm@svc(bedrock, "Foundation model") fm --> g2@svc(bedrock, "Guardrails
output check") g2 -->|answer + citations| u
bedrock.diagramCaption: RAG on Bedrock: retrieve relevant chunks from a Knowledge Base, have the model answer only from them, and wrap both ends in Guardrails.

bedrock-agentcore.diagram:
flowchart TD u[User]:::user --> rt@svc(bedrock-agentcore, "Runtime
isolated session") rt --> fm@svc(bedrock, "Model") rt <--> mem@svc(bedrock-agentcore, "Memory") rt --> gw@svc(bedrock-agentcore, "Gateway
MCP tools") id@svc(bedrock-agentcore, "Identity
OAuth tokens") -.-> gw gw --> pol[Policy check]:::sec pol --> fn@svc(lambda, "Tool Lambda") pol --> api[SaaS / internal API]:::ext pol -.->|traces| obs@svc(cloudwatch, "Observability")
bedrock-agentcore.diagramCaption: AgentCore gives agents a production harness: isolated Runtime, managed Memory, Gateway for tools with Policy enforcement, and Identity for credentials.

sagemaker-ai.diagram:
flowchart TD s3@svc(s3, "Training data") --> tr@svc(sagemaker-ai, "Training job
+ tuning") tr -->|model artifact| reg[Model registry]:::note reg --> q{"Traffic
pattern?"}:::note q -->|steady, low latency| rtep@svc(sagemaker-ai, "Real-time endpoint") q -->|spiky / idle| sl@svc(sagemaker-ai, "Serverless") q -->|large or offline| as@svc(sagemaker-ai, "Async / Batch") rtep --> mon@svc(cloudwatch, "Model Monitor")
sagemaker-ai.diagramCaption: SageMaker AI covers the custom-model lifecycle; the key design choice is the inference option that fits the traffic pattern.

amazon-q-business.diagram:
flowchart TD u[Employees]:::user -->|SSO| qb@svc(amazon-q-business) src[SharePoint, Salesforce,
S3 ...]:::ext -->|connectors| idx[Index + ACLs]:::note idx --> qb qb --> pl[Plugins: Jira ...]:::ext qb -->|only permitted
content| ans[Answer]:::user
amazon-q-business.diagramCaption: Q Business answers employees from indexed enterprise sources and only returns content each user is already allowed to see.

amazon-q-developer.diagram:
flowchart TD dev[Developer]:::user --> qd@svc(amazon-q-developer) qd --> code[Code, agents,
scans]:::note qd -.->|retiring| kiro[Kiro]:::compute kiro --> eos[EOS
Apr 30 2027]:::note
amazon-q-developer.diagramCaption: Q Developer is being retired (no new sign-ups since May 15, 2026); AWS directs developers to Kiro for agentic, spec-driven coding.

nova.diagram:
flowchart TD app@svc(lambda, "App") -->|Converse API| br@svc(bedrock) br --> lite@svc(nova, "Nova 2 Lite
fast reasoning") br --> sonic@svc(nova, "Nova 2 Sonic
speech to speech") br --> omni@svc(nova, "Nova 2 Omni
multimodal") act@svc(nova, "Nova Act
browser agents") --> web[Web UIs]:::ext forge[Nova Forge
custom training]:::note -.-> lite
nova.diagramCaption: Nova is Amazon's own model family on Bedrock: pick the model by modality and cost, and use Nova Act for UI-automation agents.

rekognition.diagram:
flowchart TD u[User upload]:::user --> s3@svc(s3, "Images / video") s3 -->|event| fn@svc(lambda) fn -->|DetectLabels,
DetectModerationLabels| rk@svc(rekognition) rk --> q{"Unsafe?"}:::note q -->|yes| rev[Human review queue]:::user q -->|no| db@svc(dynamodb, "Store labels")
rekognition.diagramCaption: Rekognition adds image and video analysis (labels, faces, moderation) through an API call, typically triggered when media lands in S3.

textract.diagram:
flowchart TD s3@svc(s3, "Scanned invoices") -->|event| fn@svc(lambda) fn -->|StartDocumentAnalysis
async| tx@svc(textract) tx -->|job done| sns@svc(sns) sns --> fn2@svc(lambda, "Parse forms
and tables") fn2 --> cm@svc(comprehend, "Entities / PII") fn2 --> db@svc(dynamodb, "Extracted fields")
textract.diagramCaption: Textract extracts text, forms and tables from documents; use the async API with an SNS notification for multi-page files.

comprehend.diagram:
flowchart TD src[Reviews, tickets]:::user --> s3@svc(s3) s3 --> cm@svc(comprehend) cm --> s1[Sentiment,
entities]:::note cm --> s2[PII]:::sec s1 --> qs@svc(quicksight, "Dashboard")
comprehend.diagramCaption: Comprehend is pre-trained NLP: sentiment, entities, PII and custom classification without building a model.

transcribe.diagram:
flowchart TD call[Call recordings]:::user --> s3@svc(s3, "Audio") s3 --> tr@svc(transcribe, "Transcribe
Call Analytics") tr --> red[PII-redacted
transcript]:::sec red --> cm@svc(comprehend, "Sentiment") red --> br@svc(bedrock, "Summarize") cm --> s3o@svc(s3, "Insights") br --> s3o
transcribe.diagramCaption: Transcribe turns speech into text (with diarization and PII redaction); downstream NLP or an LLM turns transcripts into insights.

kiro.diagram:
flowchart TD dev[Developer prompt]:::user --> k[Kiro IDE / CLI]:::compute k --> req[requirements.md
EARS stories]:::note req --> des[design.md]:::note des --> tasks[tasks.md]:::note tasks --> code[Implemented code
+ tests]:::compute hook[Agent hooks
on file save]:::note -.-> code code -->|push| cp@svc(codepipeline)
kiro.diagramCaption: Kiro works spec-first: requirements, then design, then tasks, then code, with hooks automating checks; it is the successor path to Q Developer.

sqs.diagram:
flowchart TD
  p1@svc(lambda, "Producer")
  p2@svc(ecs, "Producer")
  p1 -->|SendMessage| q@svc(sqs, "Queue")
  p2 --> q
  q -->|poll| c1@svc(lambda, "Consumer")
  q -->|poll| c2@svc(ec2, "Worker ASG")
  q -->|after maxReceiveCount| dlq@svc(sqs, "Dead-letter queue")
  dlq -.->|redrive after fix| q
  c2 -.->|scale on queue depth| cw@svc(cloudwatch)
sqs.diagramCaption: SQS buffers work between producers and consumers; failed messages move to a DLQ, and queue depth drives consumer scaling.

sns.diagram:
flowchart TD pub@svc(lambda, "Order service") -->|Publish| t@svc(sns, "Topic") t -->|filter: all| q1@svc(sqs, "Billing queue") t -->|filter: type=shipped| q2@svc(sqs, "Shipping queue") t --> more[Lambda, Firehose,
email / SMS ...]:::note q1 --> w1@svc(ecs, "Billing worker") q2 --> w2@svc(lambda, "Shipping worker")
sns.diagramCaption: SNS fans one message out to many subscribers; put an SQS queue behind each consumer so each can fail or lag independently.

eventbridge.diagram:
flowchart TD src[AWS, apps, SaaS]:::user -->|events| bus@svc(eventbridge, "Event bus") bus --> r1{"Rule:
orders > 100"}:::note bus --> r2{"Rule:
EC2 stopped"}:::note r1 --> sf@svc(step-functions) r1 --> q@svc(sqs) r2 --> sns@svc(sns)
eventbridge.diagramCaption: EventBridge routes events by content: rules match patterns on the bus and deliver to targets, with retries, DLQs and archive/replay.

step-functions.diagram:
flowchart TD
  s([Start]):::note --> v@svc(lambda, "Validate order")
  v --> pay@svc(lambda, "Charge payment")
  pay -->|Retry 3x backoff| pay
  pay --> par[Parallel]:::note
  par --> inv@svc(dynamodb, "Reserve stock")
  par --> sh@svc(sqs, "Queue shipping")
  pay -.->|Catch error| ref@svc(lambda, "Refund / compensate")
  ref --> fail([Fail]):::sec
  inv --> ok([Succeed]):::storage
  sh --> ok
step-functions.diagramCaption: Step Functions makes the workflow explicit: each state can Retry with backoff and Catch errors into compensating steps (the saga pattern).

appsync.diagram:
flowchart TD u[Web / mobile app]:::user -->|GraphQL| as@svc(appsync) cg@svc(cognito) -.->|auth| as as --> r1@svc(dynamodb, "Resolver: posts") as --> r2@svc(lambda, "Resolver: search") as --> r3@svc(aurora, "Resolver: users") r1 -.->|mutation triggers
subscription push| ws[Subscribed clients
WebSocket]:::user
appsync.diagramCaption: AppSync is one managed GraphQL endpoint that resolves fields from many data sources and pushes real-time updates via subscriptions.

mq.diagram:
flowchart TD subgraph onp[On-premises] legacy[JMS / AMQP apps]:::ext end subgraph vpc[VPC] act@svc(mq, "Active broker
AZ a") stb@svc(mq, "Standby broker
AZ b") app@svc(ec2, "Migrated app") end legacy -->|VPN / DX| act app --> act act -.->|failover| stb act --> efs@svc(efs, "Shared storage")
mq.diagramCaption: Amazon MQ lifts existing ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ apps without code changes; for new cloud-native designs prefer SQS/SNS.

iot-core.diagram:
flowchart TD dev[Devices]:::user -->|MQTT + X.509| iot@svc(iot-core) iot --> sh[Device shadow]:::note iot --> re{"Rules engine
SQL on topics"}:::note re --> kds@svc(kinesis-data-streams) re --> fn@svc(lambda, "Alerts") re --> more[Timestream, S3,
DynamoDB ...]:::note
iot-core.diagramCaption: IoT Core authenticates devices over MQTT and its rules engine routes messages to streams, databases, Lambda or S3.
